floor_history.headline: Recon baseline 18 (91 vs 91 insns, pure RA+sched). Cluster-A callee-save rotation mechanism CONFIRMED via cc1 -da: the goto-loop emits no NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG, so allocno_compare ranks the param above t

frontier.hypothesis: A loop spelling exists that emits NOTE_INSN_LOOP_BEG (flipping the allocno priorities to target's 77/76/72) while denying loop.c the hoist of the two loop-invariant compare constants 0x3C0000 and 0x1000000, landing cluster A at no instruction cost.
frontier.mechanism: tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c scan_loop / move_movables: a set(reg)(const_int) becomes a movable and is hoisted to the preheader when it survives the maybe_never test and clears threshold = (loop_has_call ? 1 : 2) * (1 + n_non_fixed_regs). This loop contains calls, so the savings bar is low and both constants get hoisted.
frontier.next_probe: Read scan_loop/move_movables for the exact suppression conditions, then probe C placements and compare spellings that make each constant a non-movable — placing the 0x3C0000 compare where maybe_never is already set, an unsigned-compare spelling that folds the threshold into the existing slt chain, and a bit-test spelling for 0x1000000 that combine keeps inline. Score each with sandbox --disable all AND re-run tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s1/greg.sh to confirm dispositions stay 77/76/72 in 16/17/18. Keep the shared-ret do-while exit shape from rejected/real-loop-confirms-ra-but-hoists-constants.c.

frontier.hypothesis: Part of cluster B (the $2<->$3 / $2<->$4 renames and the 14-entry reorder over the debug_printf argument block) is downstream of the cluster-A callee-save rotation and will shrink or vanish once the allocation is correct.
frontier.mechanism: The argument-block address chains add into the D_800A125C base register; target indexes off $s0 while our build indexes off $s1, and the scratch-register choices in the block ($a0 as the arg4 index scratch in target vs $v0/$v1 in our build) are allocated after the callee-saves are fixed.
frontier.next_probe: Once any form lands the 77/76/72 dispositions, re-run tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s1/grind_diff.py and re-score both known-equal arg-staging orders (arg4-first, the current candidate, and arg5-first, the inherited baseline) against the new allocation before doing any further arg-block work.

frontier.hypothesis: The per-allocno n_refs and live_length values behind the priority inversion can be read directly rather than inferred, which would let F1's candidate spellings be predicted instead of sampled.
frontier.mechanism: allocno_compare's inputs (allocno_n_refs, allocno_live_length) are not printed by -da; only the resulting order is. An instrumented cc1 built into tmp/ that prints both fields per allocno would make the priority arithmetic directly observable for both the goto-loop and real-loop forms.
frontier.next_probe: Build cc1 into tmp/gccdbg/ with an fprintf of allocno_n_refs/allocno_live_length at the qsort call site in global_alloc, dump both forms, and confirm which term (the floor_log2 step or the live_length divisor) actually moves the param. Dumps-for-understanding only — the shipped toolchain stays frozen.
